title: Navigating DAS Registration
description: A practical guide to getting a program and its apprentices registered in California: standards, the DAS 1 apprentice agreement, 8 CCR 206 timelines, IACA vs. CAC jurisdiction, and how intermediaries shorten the path. Sets realistic timeline expectations for employers.
notes: Audience: Business services, program managers, employers' HR partners. Format: LV. Hours assumed from format (LV = 3 hours). Gap addressed: AJCC staff have no documented role in or training on registration; intermediary studies cite roughly six-month timelines.
learning_objectives: Outline the steps and documents required to register a new program and an apprentice.
Determine which advisory body has jurisdiction over a program.
Set an accurate timeline expectation with an employer.
Decide when to use an existing intermediary program instead of registering a new one.

sequencing_rationale: Lessons follow the catalog's learning objectives in the order a practitioner meets them on the job: Registration Steps and Documents; IACA vs. CAC Jurisdiction; Setting an Honest Timeline with an Employer; When to Use an Existing Intermediary Program. The closing project ("Project: Registration Roadmap for a Sample Employer") applies the earlier lessons to one realistic work product (a registration roadmap for a sample employer covering documents, jurisdiction, a realistic timeline, and a register-or-join decision) rather than introducing new content. Scope assumptions: hours are not stated in the source catalog and are assumed from the delivery format (LV; LV = 3 hours). Content is grounded in California and federal guidance named in the catalog description and objectives; the course cites those directives by number but does not reproduce their text, and every policy-specific claim must be checked against the current directive before delivery. Local board policy is treated as a variable the learner fills in from their own board, not something the course prescribes. Design driver (catalog "gap addressed"): AJCC staff have no documented role in or training on registration; intermediary studies cite roughly six-month timelines. Statistics and audit findings quoted from the catalog have not been independently verified. Prerequisites reflect track order: APP 101 (Registered Apprenticeship for Workforce Professionals).
